one_liner: Project manager in NNSA's nuclear nonproliferation office, running budgets, plans and metrics and coordinating with national labs, contractors and international and interagency partners.
fit_summary: Daniel's IEM consulting background likely brings government-client program support and stakeholder coordination, and Daniel's policy knowledge and relationship skills match the 'Stakeholder Management' and 'Partnering' competencies. The hard part is the specialized experience, which requires a year at GS-11 level supporting national security and foreign policy objectives through international engagement. Domestic emergency-management work may not clearly meet that bar unless Daniel's IEM work touched international, interagency, or national-security programs.
eligibility: Open to the public (excepted service). U.S. citizenship is required, and no federal status is needed.

Specialized experience: at least one year equivalent to GS-11/EN-00 supporting U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives through international engagement, stakeholder coordination, and program execution.

0130 basic requirement: 24 semester hours in political science, international relations, history, economics, or similar fields; or a qualifying combination of education and experience; or four years of foreign-affairs-related experience. Confirm your transcript qualifies.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Q clearance. Drug testing, a financial disclosure, and a 2-year trial period also apply.
Your resume must be no more than two pages, or you will be disqualified. HR reviews only the first two pages.
strategy: Mark the window: the posting opens Oct 28 and closes Nov 4, 2026, which gives you only one week. Draft your two-page resume and preview the questionnaire at the USA Staffing link beforehand.

Frame IEM work as program execution for government clients. Name the federal, state, or local agencies you supported, along with the budget, plan, schedule, and metrics duties you held, and use the exact competency words.

Surface any international, homeland-security, or interagency elements. Examples include FEMA/DHS coordination, multi-agency exercises, and briefing senior officials; tie these to national security where it is honest to do so.

In each job entry, list start and end dates (month/year) and hours per week. Make sure every questionnaire answer is supported by a specific resume line, since the posting forbids writing 'see resume.'
Confirm your 0130 education basis now: count your political science, history, and economics credits. Have your transcripts ready, because official copies are required if you are selected.
If your experience is mostly domestic, consider applying in parallel to emergency-management or policy roles where your fit is stronger.
resume_bullets: Managed [program/project] for [government client] at IEM, developing project plans, tracking [number] milestones and metrics, and supporting a $[amount] annual budget.
Coordinated with [number] federal, state, and local stakeholders, including [agencies], to plan and execute [exercise/initiative], building partnerships that [result].
Prepared analysis and recommendations for [senior leaders/client executives] on [preparedness/security topic], informing [decision or outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a project you managed from planning through execution. How did you track progress and handle budget changes?
Tell us about coordinating with multiple stakeholders who had competing priorities, such as labs, contractors, or agencies.
How does your experience connect to supporting U.S. national security or foreign policy objectives?
Give an example of a recommendation you made to senior leadership and how it was received.
watch_outs: The one-week application window is easy to miss.
The specialized experience requires international or foreign-policy engagement, and domestic emergency-management experience alone may be rated not qualified.
You must be able to obtain a Q clearance, which involves a long investigation. Telework is not available, so expect an onsite daily commute from Manassas to DC.
Resumes over two pages are disqualified.
